display.title: Tanya Chapter 36, Part 2: Moshiach, Techiyas HaMeisim and the Preview at Sinai
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur finishing chapter 36: the days of Moshiach and Techiyas HaMeisim are the goal of this world, and Hashem gave a preview of them at Matan Torah.
display.summary_long: The second class on Tanya chapter 36 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish series. It recaps why there are four worlds, matching the four letters of Hashem's name and the many mitzvos that come in fours, and why all the countless worlds exist for the sake of this physical one. A miner brought out of long darkness must have his eyes covered; so too the soul needs the Torah's strength to bear the great revelation of Moshiach. The Alter Rebbe then teaches that the days of Moshiach, and above all Techiyas HaMeisim, are the purpose and perfection of this world, when the body will be so refined that it gives life to the soul. A talk follows on the Frierdiker Rebbe's letter in Hayom Yom: every day a Jew should ask what he has done to bring Moshiach closer, as Avraham Avinu accounted for each of his days. The main reward comes in the seventh millennium. Just as a baby's soul is taught the whole Torah before birth as a preview, Hashem showed the Jewish people a taste of the future at Matan Torah, when they 'saw the sounds', and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev taught that on Shabbos Chazon every Jew is shown the third Beis HaMikdash. The recording breaks off as a story of the Baal Shem Tov begins.
display.lesson: The whole world was made for the days of Moshiach, so each day we should ask ourselves what we have done in deed, word and thought to bring Moshiach closer.
